evals.prompt: We have a RAG assistant that answers HR policy questions for Acme's 3,000 employees from a 400-page handbook. We're about to swap the model and rewrite the system prompt. We have about 1,200 real logged questions from the last quarter, and HR has hand-labeled 80 of them with correct answers. The answer that hurts most is confidently wrong parental-leave or termination guidance. Design the eval harness so we don't ship a regression.
assertions: The golden set is split into representative, adversarial/edge, and regression buckets, with a case count and sourcing stated for each
Representative cases are drawn from the 1,200 logged questions and 80 HR labels the user supplied; any synthetic or model-generated cases are flagged as weak evidence
Each bucket or case names its grading method, and programmatic or structured-assertion checks are preferred over LLM-as-judge where the output is checkable
If an LLM judge is used (e.g. for faithfulness), it has its own rubric, is validated against the HR human labels, and controls for position, verbosity, and self-preference bias
The metric, the no-regression gate against baseline, and a critical subset (parental-leave and termination answers) held at 100% are all set before any run
A held-out split is defined and the rule against tuning on the test set is stated explicitly
Cost per run and p95 latency are tracked alongside the quality metric
A failure taxonomy (e.g. hallucination, refusal, missed-edge-case) is defined so iteration targets the biggest bucket
